architecture_scope: The task-state interfaces must remain reusable across raid sizes, difficulties, bosses, dungeons, and roles; Magmaw parasite control is only the first vertical slice.

first_broken_edge.cause: The actor-specific combat contract permits parasite targets only for the fixed Mage/Hunter bait pair, and the local parasite-escape policy returns immediately for every non-baiter. A pursued non-baiter therefore cannot attack the threat or emit its own Survival escape.

next_action: Allow ordinary DPS to attack only a personally threatening parasite and allow every pursued bot to emit one persistent local Survival escape, while keeping the fixed Mage/Hunter pair as the only bait-lane owners. Validate once in compiled replays; do not build or start a server.

allowed: actor-specific Magmaw parasite target eligibility for a DPS actor personally threatened by a live parasite
a persistent per-bot local escape candidate for any role personally threatened by a parasite
fixed Fire Mage and Marksman Hunter bait assignments and lane-transfer ownership unchanged
exposed-head targeting remains strictly above parasite and boss targeting
ordinary native spell range, line of sight, GCD, resource, target, cast, and movement legality
focused compiled owner/non-owner target and movement replays through the shared production adapter and real action kernel
one implementation and one matched verification run
forbidden: bot-side Z adjustment, vertical steering, target-height normalization, teleportation, MMAP tolerance, fallback fraction, route coordinate, or global movement-planner changes
changing the fixed Mage/Hunter bait pair or granting lane ownership to a non-baiter
class rotation, coefficient, pet, consumable, healer triage, tank threat, encounter script, SQL, or roster changes
enabling persistent task authority by default or promoting live fixture revisions 9/8/8
unconditionally focusing remote parasites, moving the whole ranged group, or treating action submission as progress
configure, build, worldserver start, authserver start, live retry, DVC publication, or gameplay-clear claim

acceptance: the exposed head remains the first damage target for every DPS actor
the Mage and Hunter remain the only bait-lane owners and retain their sticky lane destination
an ordinary DPS selects a parasite only when that parasite personally threatens the actor and is within the existing legal encounter target envelope
a pursued non-baiter emits one actor-owned Survival escape with stable identity and destination until measured safety or terminal failure
a safe non-baiter neither acquires lane movement nor abandons Magmaw for a remote parasite
focused compiled replays pass through the shared production adapter and real action kernel
authority remains default-off and native pathing remains the sole owner of terrain elevation
